Actually supermemory.ai has a very distinctive design: it's mostly plain white background with black text, serif/mono mix? Let me look at their console too (console.supermemory.ai). But console requires login.

Supermemory's design language (from memory + the fetched text): The site is extremely minimal — white background, black text, system-ish sans, thin borders, a lot of plain text, diagrams as inline SVG with labels like "learner-1", "memory db". Their landing is known for being sparse: large headline text, monospace annotations, minimal chrome, no gradients, no rounded card shadows. And the console (console.supermemory.ai) has a left sidebar with workspace switcher, tabs like "Overview / Memories / Graph / Connectors / API Keys", light gray background, subtle borders, small text, tables with monospace IDs.

I should actually inspect the real thing more concretely — fetch CSS or take a screenshot. I can open the page in the browser (preview_open) and take a screenshot to look at it. That's allowed — the user explicitly asked "match the supermemory.ai ui", which requires visual inspection. Actually the guidance says take screenshots only when the user explicitly asks for a screenshot or visual check. Here, matching a UI implies visual analysis of the reference. This is a case where visual inspection is needed and justified. I'll open supermemory.ai in the browser and screenshot it to extract the design tokens (colors, fonts, spacing, borders).

Also let me check the docs folder for design notes and the console pages. And check what the app currently looks like.

Let me plan: 
1. Inspect supermemory.ai visually (landing + maybe docs/console).
2. Inventory the app's UI surfaces: public landing (landing.tsx, product-landing.tsx), docs hub, pricing, login/signup, demo, console pages (overview, events, journeys, settings, dashboard), components/ui.
3. Restyle globally: globals.css tokens + a shared design system, then update shell + pages.

This is a big task. Let me first gather. Also note the repo has apps/ and packages/ dirs.

Now the plan. The app is 7137 lines of TSX across many custom styles using Tailwind arbitrary values with sky/blue palettes, cream landing, etc. Making the *full application* match requires a systematic restyle:

1. Global tokens in globals.css: replace sky palette with supermemory tokens (paper/ink/blue, hairlines, radius, Geist fonts via next/font or Google Fonts import).
2. Tailwind config: add font families and color tokens so components can use them; but existing components use arbitrary hex values heavily. The most effective approach: define CSS overrides? No — better to rewrite the design at the token/class level.

Given the size, I need to be strategic: I'll build a design system layer in globals.css (component classes: surface, panel, btn, status-pill, eyebrow, inputs, tables) using supermemory tokens, load Geist + Geist Mono via next/font/google, then update the layouts and pages to use those classes/tokens instead of sky colors. But many components use inline Tailwind classes like `bg-sky-50 text-sky-700` etc. A complete match would require touching every component. 7137 lines is a lot but doable with targeted replacements? Risky.

Alternative pragmatic approach that yields genuine full-app consistency: use Tailwind config to remap the `sky` palette to supermemory blues, and `slate` to ink greys; override rounded-* radii? That's hacky but very effective for a "match the UI" task across an entire app. Hmm, but "match the supermemory.ai ui" means also the structure/aesthetic: square corners, hairline borders, mono uppercase labels, 400-weight headings, flat surfaces (no gradients/glows/translate hover).

Actually the current app is the opposite aesthetic: glossy light-blue, gradients, rounded-2xl, glows, hover translate. The landing uses cream Fraunces serif (which is closer to old supermemory). The responsive pass is done. I audited every route in a real browser at 320, 375, 390, 768, 1440 and 1440+ widths, measuring `scrollWidth` against `clientWidth` to catch overflow rather than eyeballing it.

**What was actually broken and fixed**

- **Console chrome** — [app-shell.tsx](components/app-shell.tsx) stacked *two* sticky bars on mobile (a brand bar plus the breadcrumb header), eating ~104px of a phone viewport. The duplicate is gone; the brand mark now sits inline in the single console header, so there is one 53px bar. The public nav also wrapped "Sign in" and "Get started" onto two lines at 360px and overflowed the page at 320px — nav items are now `whitespace-nowrap`/`shrink-0`, and the inline sign-in link hides below 360px while appearing in the hamburger menu.
- **Overview AI bar** — [overview-product.tsx](components/overview-product.tsx) had the "Ask Gemini" button absolutely positioned over the input's placeholder on phones. It now becomes a full-width button below the field on mobile, an icon-only button on tablet (where it previously covered the placeholder text), and the labelled button on desktop. The chat widget's fixed `w-96` also overflowed a 375px screen; it's now inset `left-3 right-3` with a `100dvh`-capped height and reverts to the corner panel at `sm`. The page header also broke into a tall stacked column at tablet width, so its row breakpoint moved to `lg`.
- **Journey detail** — [app/journeys/[userId]/page.tsx](app/journeys/[userId]/page.tsx) had "Last action:" splitting mid-word, the recommendation label squeezing body text into a narrow ragged column, "6 steps" collapsing vertically beside the timeline heading, and a fixed 26px user ID. All now wrap or stack, with the ID scaling down at mobile.
- **Scroll tab strips** — [globals.css](app/globals.css) referenced a `scrollbar-none` utility that never existed, so the docs tab rail showed a chunky grey scrollbar on mobile. The utility is now defined.
- **Landing** — [app/page.tsx](app/page.tsx) hero drops to 36px at the smallest widths, and the announcement dot aligns to the first line instead of floating beside a wrapped block.

**Verification** — `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, and `npx next build` all pass. I exercised the real console as a signed-in user (simulated events, journey cards, expanded payloads, sidebar drawer, AI drawer) and confirmed no horizontal overflow on landing, pricing, docs (all tabs), signup, signin, overview, events, journeys, journey detail and settings. The throwaway review account and its demo telemetry were deleted afterward. The dev server is running at `http://127.0.0.1:3000` (pid 56736) and registered in the preview panel.

One note: `components/workspace.tsx`, `product-landing.tsx`, `landing.tsx` and `intelligence-dashboard.tsx` aren't imported by any route, so they were left untouched — they still contain the old cream palette and won't inherit these fixes.

The obvious next step is a phone-sized pass over the empty and error states, which I could only see partially with fresh accounts.
